newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends sharply lower on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends sharply lower on USDA report.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed broadly lower on fund selling tied to bearishness over the USDA September crop report, traders said.

USDA raised 1996-97 wheat ending stocks to 506 million bushels from the August forecast for 409 million bushels. The report also raised the estimate of the Australian wheat crop to 19.5 million bushels from 17.5 million bushels forecast previously.

"The USDA numbers underscored the market's feeling that world crops are going to be bigger than we thought. That accelerated the technical downtrend that we've seen in here for the last couple of weeks," a trader said.

KCBT wheat closed 10 to 15-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with Sept down 12 cents at $4.43 a bushel. Dec lost 15-1/4 cents to close at $4.36-3/4 -- a little more than two cents above the contract low at $4.34-1/2. March ended at a new low of $4.32 per bushel, down 15-1/4 cents on the day.
Traders said Prudential Securities sold three million Dec bushels. Refco and LFG each sold at least 2.3 million Dec. CIS bought 2.2 million Dec and a million July, floor sources said.
KCBT estimated Wednesday's wheat volume at 38.285 million bushels, above Tuesday's volume of 22.75 million bushels.
